sentences.text:
The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (DAR) filed under section 159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after called as 'Act') by the investigating officer of FIR No.198/2019 Police Station PIA, Delhi.
2.
The accident in the present case took place on 26.11.2019.

As per the facts narrated in FIR and charge-sheet, injured petitioner Ram Babu (now deceased) alongwith his son namely Santosh had come to Anand Vihar Bus Terminal to board the bus for going to Mainpuri, U.P. and was standing at counter No. 114.

It is further mentioned that at about 8 pm, one roadways bus bearing registration No. UP-81BT-0627, being driven by its driver at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came from parking side and hit the petitioner Ram Babu from left side, as a result of which he fell down on road and rear tyre of the bus ran over his left leg.
Thereafter, PCR Van took him to Max Hospital.
The driver of the offending vehicle ran away from the spot after leaving the bus.
In this connection, an FIR No. 0198 was registered at PS PIA.
3. Both respondents have marked appearance and filed their separate written statements.

3.1 In the written statement filed by R-1 /driver, it is stated that he has been falsely implicated in the present accident, while he has nothing to do with the said accident and no accident took place due to the negligence or rash driving of R-1.
Rest of the averments have been denied.
3.2 R-2 / UPSRTC has filed its separate written statement and it is stated that case is liable to be dismissed as the accident did not occur due to the fault of the respondent and its employee.

It is submitted that as per the information, on the date of accident, the employee of R-2 was going to park the bus bearing registration No. UP-81BT-0627 at counter No. 112 for plying on the route from Anand Vihar Delhi to Kasganj at normal speed by following traffic rules and regulations and on that day Santosh Kumar was the conductor of the bus.
It is further submitted that at that moment, an old person collided with an unknown person and fell down on the road and came in contact of the bus.
It is submitted that the alleged accident did not take place due to the fault of the employee of answering respondent and R-2 was falsely implicated in the present case by the IO and the petitioner.
Rest of the averments of the FIR are denied.

4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed on 23.03.2023 :-
(i) Whether the petitioner Ram Babu suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident that happened on 26.11.2019 at 8:00 pm near Counter No. 114, ISBT, Anand Vihar, Delhi, within jurisdiction fo PS PIA, due to rash and negligent driving of bus bearing registration No. UP-81BT-0627 being driven by respondent No.1/ Sunit Kumar ?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled to the compensation on account of said injuries,
if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP)

He relied upon the following documents :-

Copy of pass book of deponent is Ex.PW1/B (OSR)

6.1 Respondent No.1 / driver of the offending vehicle has stepped into witness box and deposed on the strength of affidavit of evidence Ex.R1W1/A. 6.2

Sh. Santosh Kumar, conductor of offending bus has been examined on behalf of R-2 / UPSRTC who deposed on the strength of affidavit of evidence Ex.R2W1/A and relied upon photocopy of his I.D. card Ex.R2W1/1.
7.

I have heard Sh. Ravendra Kumar, Ld. counsel for petitioners and Sh. Pradeep Kumar Gupta, Ld.
Counsel for R2 / UPSRTC.
I have perused the record.
8. The issues are decided as follows:-

ISSUE No.1 :
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities, which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further, in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
10. Now in this case, Santosh, son of the deceased is examined as eye witness to the accident and he has been examined as PW1.
He clearly deposed regarding manner of accident and involvement of offending vehicle in the same.
He deposed regarding rash and negligent driving of bus by rider/R1.

He testified that on the date of accident i.e. 26.11.2019, he alongwith his father Ram Babu (
petitioner now deceased) had come inside Anand Vihar Bus stand and was standing to reach Mainpuri at Counter No. 114 and at about 8 pm, a bus bearing registration No. IP-81BT-0627 being driven by its driver at a very high speed and rash and negligent manner, came from parking side and hit his father from the left side of the bus, due to which his father fell down on road and his left leg came under the front tyre of the bus and he received grievous injuries.
Thereafter, he was taken to Max Hospital by PCR vehicle.
He was cross-examined at length by Ld. Counsel for R-2 but nothing fruitful has come out which could shatter the case of the petitioner.

FIR was registered on the very next day of the date of accident in the intervening night of 26.11.2019 & 27.11.2019 without any Rambabu vs Sumit on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120401610/

sentences.text: unreasonable delay and number of offending vehicle was clearly mentioned in the FIR itself.
Complaint was made to the police on the same day by petitioner Santosh, who is also eye witness in this case and FIR was registered wihtin 4 hours from the time of accident at 8:00 pm on 26.11.2019.
PW1 deposed that offending bus was coming from wrong side.

During his cross-examination, a suggestion was given to R1W1 / driver of the offending vehicle that he has not given any complaint to the police of his false implication, which he affirmed in positive.
It is also to be kept in mind that R-1 and R-2 have not disputed the presence of offending vehicle at the spot and merely disputed its involvement.

The standard of proof applicable in the cases of accidental claim before MACT is of preponderance of probabilities and once the testimony of eye witnesss is on record and no serious dent could be made in his testimony by any of the respondents by leading any evidence to the contrary, in my considered view, a view favourable to the injured has to be taken by the Tribunal.

Final opinion on the MLC of the petitioner with respect to nature of injuries was given as 'grievous'.
11.

In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge- sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.

12. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and discussion above-said, it is proved that the injured Ram Babu received grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Petitioners have been able to prove that Ram Babu received grievous injuries in the accident.
Accordingly, with these observations, these issues are accordingly decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.

ISSUE No.2 :
13.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
14. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

sentences.text:
Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the now deceased petitioner Ram Babu, the compensation is awarded in favour of substituted petitioners (LRs of injured petitioner Ram Babu (since deceased)) under the aforesaid heads as follows :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
16.
PW1 / Santosh, (son /one of LRs of deceased Ram Babu) has relied on certain medical bills /documents / pharmacy bills Mark A (20 pages) of deceased petitioner Ram Babu.
Most of the pharmacy bills do not bear any signature or stamp.

The discharge summary of Ram Babu for a period of hospitalization from 17.02.2020 to 21.02.2020 is on record and shows that he was taken to the hospital with complaint of sudden onset seizure episode with loss of consciousness and diagnosed with one episode of LOC likely seizure.
He is a known case of Cornory artery disease with Lvef 40% observed during course in the hospital.
There is nothing to relate the treatment under question with accidental injuries, even though history of RTA was reported to the doctor.
There is nothing in the discharge summary to relate the seizure with accidental injuries in left ankle.

It is clear from the discharge summary that the hospitalization above stated was not with respect to the injuries sustained in the accident and hence, any of the Medical bills for the said period cannot be considered by the Tribunal.

Moving further, petitioner has relied on pharmacy bill of the period from 22.04.2020 to 15.11.2020 but no corresponding treatment papers have been annexed to co-relate the bills to the injuries sustained in the accident and hence these pharmacy bills cannot be considered by the Tribunal.

PW Santosh who is petitioner No.1 now, admitted in his cross-examination that death of his father was due to natural causes and not due to accidental injuries and the medical documents of Arogya Hospital shows that death was natural.
Late petitioner Ram Babu was admitted to Max hospital for the period 26.11.2019 to 02.12.2019 in relation to the treatment due to accidental injuries.
PW Santosh deposed in his cross-examination that "My father was taken to Max Hospitial, Patparganj.
It is correct that all medical bills were paid by ECHS (Ex-servicemen contributory Health Scheme) and Delhi Arogya Kosh and there was no medical expenses borne by petitioner Ram Babu".

The MLC of the petitioner shows that he had sustained crush injuries in his left foot and the medical bills as relied on in the calculation sheet relied on by the petitioner as Ex.PW1/C, many of the invoices pertain to prior to date of accident and many pertain to the year 2020 and there is no such medical prescription/treatment paper corresponding to those bills as relating to the accidental injuries in question.

It is clear from the testimony of PW1 Santosh that deceased was an Ex-serviceman and his treatment expenses post accident were paid by ECHS and Delhi Arogya Kosh and no medical expenses were borne by the original petitioner Ram Babu.

Petitioner has filed another break up of medical bills dated 23.08.2025 but it is strange that in it also he has claimed for several invoices (like dated 02.08.2019,28.08.2019,10.10.2019 etc.) prior to the date of accident i.e.26.11.2019 and there is no explanation in this regard.
As discussed above, as petitioner Santosh has himself accepted that no medical expenses were met in the treatment post accident, there is no question for any payment under this head.

In the written submissions, petitioners have stated that expenses incurred on treatment as paid by late petitioner was Rs.55,091/- but this amount also does not tally with any of the break-up of medical bills filed by petitioner side and does not clarify which bill under reference was paid by the petitioner personally.
Under this head, only original medical bills are reimbursed.
Hence, no amount of money is being awarded under this head.

In case titled Tejinder Pal Singh Vs. Gurmail Singh Thekedar, FAO No. 373/1990 decided on 03.02.2011 (2011 SCC online P& H 2024), it was held that :-

sentences.text: During the pendency of appeal, the appellant has died and legal representative have been added.
Since the petition had already been dismissed by the tribunal, the component of pain & Sufferings could not survive to the legal representative.
If an award had already been passed and it had been granted to the claimant, it would have survived to the estate for a legal representative to claim.

In terms of section 306 of the Indian Succession Act, a compensation for personal injury shall not survive for consideration by the legal representative, if it had not been already determined before the death of a person".
18.
In the case at hand, petitioner Ram Babu died during the pendency of the claim petition / DAR filed by IO and hence, claim under this head does not survive.
Hence, no amount is being granted under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 19.
The petitioners have not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.

However, it is seen that injured Ram Babu suffered from grievous injuries and had repeated visits to the hospital in connection with accidental injuries and treatment at hospital and his further medication was continuing.
Hence, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards conveyance as Ram Babu / his family must have borne considerable expenses towards his visits to hospital.

Considering the advance age and injuries suffered by original petitioner Ram Babu, it can reasonably be assumed that he must have required good diet for recovery and must have incurred expenses towards it.
Hence, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards special diet.

20. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioners or late Ram Babu had hired any attendant during treatment of Ram Babu, considering that he had sustained grievous injuries and fracture at advance age of 75 years, it cannot be ignored that family members of Ram Babu must have had to render their services for providing assistance to him for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded as attendant charges.

21. Thus, petitioners are granted a total compensation of Rs.60,000/- (20,000+20,000+20,000)
under this head.

sentences.text: PW1 did not depose a single word on the aspect of Loss of income during treatment.
During his cross-examination, he asserted that his father had retired from Indian Army.
The deceased Ram Babu was a senior citizen, 75 years of age.
There is absolutely nothing to suggest that he had any post retirement avocation in life as generating income.

In written submissions, though it is stated that late petitioner Ram Babu was working as farmer post-retirement and having income from agricultural land, neither any loss of earning is proved nor any loss of income is pleaded by petitioner.
Thus, in my considered view, as there was no loss of income during treatment, no amount is being granted under this head.

LIABILITY:
25.
Since the offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident and the respondent No.2 is UPSRTC, thus, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities, which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
It is also to be kept in mind that R-1 and R-2 have not disputed the presence of offending vehicle at the spot and merely disputed its involvement.
The standard of proof applicable in the cases of accidental claim before MACT is of preponderance of probabilities and once the testimony of eye witnesss is on record and no serious dent could be made in his testimony by any of the respondents by leading any evidence to the contrary, in my considered view, a view favourable to the injured has to be taken by the Tribunal.
In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.
If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that charge- sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
12. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and discussion above-said, it is proved that the injured Ram Babu received grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Petitioners have been able to prove that Ram Babu received grievous injuries in the accident.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
There is nothing to relate the treatment under question with accidental injuries, even though history of RTA was reported to the doctor.
There is nothing in the discharge summary to relate the seizure with accidental injuries in left ankle.
It is clear from the discharge summary that the hospitalization above stated was not with respect to the injuries sustained in the accident and hence, any of the Medical bills for the said period cannot be considered by the Tribunal.
Moving further, petitioner has relied on pharmacy bill of the period from 22.04.2020 to 15.11.2020 but no corresponding treatment papers have been annexed to co-relate the bills to the injuries sustained in the accident and hence these pharmacy bills cannot be considered by the Tribunal.
Hence, no amount of money is being awarded under this head.
